title: CAP-M3 · Deploy & Docs Check
subject: system-design
description:
Capstone Sprint 3: polish, deploy and document. Freeze features by mid-week; anything new goes to a future scope slide, not the codebase. By the end of the week your capstone runs on a public URL and is documented well enough for a recruiter to understand it in two minutes. This is a formative checkpoint before Demo Day; it does not count towards the capstone grade.

MUST (in your team's capstone repo)
1. Live deployment: front end, back end and a separate production database (or a hosted Streamlit / Spaces app for data and AI projects), loaded with synthetic demo data and demo accounts for each role. The smoke test passes: HTTPS, health check, each role logs in, main journey works, inner pages refresh.
2. README per the project documentation checklist: title and one-line description, live URL, demo video link, problem, features, screenshots, stack, setup instructions that work on a fresh clone (with .env.example), demo accounts, folder structure, team contributions, future scope.
3. docs/architecture.png updated to match what you actually built.
4. docs/api.md (endpoints with auth, request, response and error codes) or, for data and AI projects, a pipeline and model document; plus docs/user-guide.md with task-based steps per role.
5. A 3-minute demo video of the live app, linked at the top of the README.
6. docs/security-checklist.md with every item marked done and a note of how: no secrets in Git, hashed passwords, parameterised queries, server-side validation and access checks, safe error messages, restricted CORS.
7. Draft Demo Day slide deck (link in the README or docs/).

SAP case-study teams: replace the live URL with a demonstrable system walkthrough or guided simulation, and the API docs with the business blueprint and test scripts.

SUBMIT: every team member submits the same repo URL. Notes: live URL, demo video link, demo account usernames (never real passwords), and the documentation sections you wrote.

rubric.title: Live deployment
rubric.description: Public URL works over HTTPS with seeded demo data and demo accounts; separate production database; smoke test passes, including refreshing inner pages.

rubric.title: README and architecture diagram
rubric.description: README follows the documentation checklist and its setup steps work on a fresh clone; the architecture diagram matches the deployed system.

rubric.title: API / user docs
rubric.description: API reference (or pipeline document) matches the running code, with error codes; the user guide gives task-based steps for each role.

rubric.title: Demo video
rubric.description: About 3 minutes, scripted, shows the main journey in the live app, states the problem and architecture briefly, and is linked in the README.

rubric.title: Security checklist
rubric.description: Checklist complete with evidence: no secrets in Git, hashed passwords, parameterised queries, server-side validation and access control, safe error handling.
